floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 8 -> 6 by folding p into multi-set base (removes load-late launch priority; index reg now matches target); residual is one 3-insn block move (base lw vs sh/andi/sra cluster), fully schedu

frontier.hypothesis: The exact dependence/priority ranking that emits sh/andi/sra ahead of the lw macro can be read from cc1 -da .sched/.sched2 dumps, and a C spelling exists that flips that one ranking
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 list scheduler orders by INSN_PRIORITY (longest path to end, ties by source order); the residual is a single 3-insn block transposition, so one priority or dependence edge decides it
frontier.next_probe: cc1 -da on the V1 .i (sandbox src/main.c), extract the func_80087D10 region of .sched and .sched2 dumps into tmp/grind/func_80087D10/s2/, identify the deciding edge and which pass moves the lw, then enumerate spellings targeting it

frontier.hypothesis: A legitimate C spelling exists where the store address stays reg-opaque at sched time (forcing sh to stay after the possibly-aliasing lw) yet still emits the direct $at-macro sh after reload
frontier.mechanism: sched1 cannot disambiguate a (mem (reg)) store against the reg+symbol table load, preserving source order; reload's REG_EQUIV substitution would restore the direct form - plain single-use pointer measured dead (cse folds first), so candidates must defeat the cse fold without dead code
frontier.next_probe: Sweep multi-set / non-constant-foldable pointer spellings; vet every candidate against the cheat catalog (pointer-alias family = sanctioned-with-prereqs) before proposing

frontier.hypothesis: Directed permuter from the V1 base (score 6, 18-insn leaf) finds the order-flipping spelling cheaply
frontier.mechanism: Residual is one block move; permuter mutation space over decls/expressions covers spellings manual enumeration misses
frontier.next_probe: permuter_campaign.py on V1 base with clean single-function target.o, fresh-seed discipline, wait/harvest in-turn
